def: Running two versions of an ad, email or page at the same time to see which one gets more leads. Change one thing at a time or you won't know what made the difference.
Whether AI assistants like ChatGPT or Google's AI answers mention your store when a shopper asks about buying a car in your area.
The share of leads that agree to a specific appointment time. One of the clearest signs of how good your first reply is.
The share of set appointments where the customer actually shows up. Confirmations and a real reason to come in push it up.
Working out which marketing channel gets credit for a lead or a sale. Never perfect — aim for consistent, not exact.
Business development centre — the team or person who answers internet leads and phone calls and books appointments.
The share of visitors who land on a page and leave without doing anything else. High bounce on vehicle pages usually means slow load times or missing info.
Searches that include your store's name. Cheap to win and important to protect, but most of those shoppers were already heading your way.
Canada's anti-spam legislation. It sets rules for consent and unsubscribing on commercial emails and texts sent to people in Canada.
The share of leads, or of shown appointments, that buy. Always say which one you mean — they are very different numbers.
Marketing aimed at shoppers who haven't picked your store yet, including people looking at a competitor's brand or models.
Money from the manufacturer that pays back part of a franchise dealer's advertising, as long as the ads follow the brand's rules.
Google's measures of how fast and stable a page feels to a real visitor. Part of why a slow dealer site can rank lower.
Total marketing spend divided by the cars sold from it. A better measure than cost per lead, because cheap leads that never buy aren't cheap.
Customer relationship management — the system that stores leads, customers, notes and follow-up tasks. Only as good as what gets entered into it.
Click-through rate — the share of people who see an ad or search result and click it.
How long a vehicle has been in stock. For used units, the listing quality has as much to do with it as the price.
Finding customers whose vehicle is worth more than what they owe, then offering them an upgrade that keeps their payment close.
Information customers gave you directly — your CRM, service history and email list. Increasingly the most valuable data a store has.
The service, parts and body shop side of the dealership. Usually more customer visits than sales sees in a month.
A limit on how many times one person sees your ad in a set period, so retargeting doesn't turn into following people around.
Your free listing on Google Search and Maps — hours, photos, reviews, posts and departments. Often the first thing a shopper sees.
How long it takes from a lead arriving to a real person replying. Track the median by day of week, not the average.
Facebook and Instagram ads with a built-in form. More leads at a lower cost, but often softer ones — plan for fast follow-up.
The three businesses Google shows with a map for local searches like "Hyundai dealer near me". Most of the calls go to these three.
A group of people a platform finds who resemble your existing customers. Built from your buyer list, it usually beats broad interest targeting.
Another name for the local pack.
Testing your own store as a shopper would: submit a lead, call, text, and score what happens.
Visitors who arrive from unpaid search results.
Pay-per-click advertising, like Google Ads, where you pay each time someone clicks.
Showing ads to people who already visited your website. Works best with a short window and real, live inventory.
How many new reviews you get each month. Recent, steady reviews matter as much as your total count.
Hidden labels in your website's code that tell search engines and AI tools exactly what each piece of information is — hours, address, vehicles, reviews.
Search engine optimization — making your website and listings easy for Google (and AI tools) to find, understand and recommend.
Turning service customers into vehicle buyers, usually by spotting good equity or big repair estimates during a service visit.
How fast a new lead gets a real, human reply. Inside ten minutes during business hours is the target.
Leads bought from or delivered by listing sites and lead providers, rather than coming to your own website.
Short labels added to the end of a link so your analytics can tell which campaign or listing a visitor came from.
Vehicle detail page — the page for one specific vehicle on your website. Where most shopping decisions actually happen.
Vehicle listing ads — Google ads that show a specific vehicle's photo, price and details right in the search results.
A search where the shopper gets their answer on Google or from an AI assistant without clicking any website.
